subject: Token savings projection & prefetch strategy — post-demo deal deck
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Davis <ben.davis@acmeco.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Token savings projection & prefetch strategy — post-demo deal deck

Ben—thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can model a clean proposal for your procurement team.

Key takeaways from today's call:
- Primary workload: fielding customer support assist and proactive suggestions inside Acme's mobile app (chat + single-turn summarization).
- Expected activity window: 100k DAUs during launch months, with estimated 1.4 million monthly active endpoints (sessions) across channels.
- Average prompt (input+output tokens): ~220 tokens per request; concurrent sessions vary but typical sequence length 250–350 tokens.
- Requirement: 99th percentile latency under 400ms for core flows; willing to accept higher latencies for background batch jobs.
- Procurement target: Acme is aiming for an effective cost target in the neighborhood of $700 per 1M tokens after caching.

What we need from you to finalize the pricing workbook:
1) Confirm monthly token volume (or range). You mentioned 180–300M tokens/month initially — can you narrow to a best estimate for Q3?
2) Typical session pattern: percentage of repeat prefixes per session (e.g., greeting + product-context) — any telemetry you can share helps our prefix-hit modeling.
3) Appetite for a short pilot (6 weeks) that enables aggressive prefix prefetching and measuring real hit rates before committing to reserved capacity.

Proposed next step: we'll run two modeled scenarios and share a short deal deck + workbook by EOD tomorrow:
- Scenario A: conservative prefix hit (30%), session-level warm cache (short TTL)
- Scenario B: aggressive prefix prefetch (60%), multi-request warm layer with longer TTL for authenticated users

I've attached the draft deck and will drop a workbook that lays out effective $/1M token under both scenarios (assumptions are editable). Please reply with the answers above or flag anything I misunderstood. If it helps, we can also schedule a 30-minute procurement sync next week.

Best,

—Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
Attachment: Deal_Deck_Acme.pdf (PDF, 1.2 MB)
Attachment: Redwood_Token_Savings_Workbook_V1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 95 KB)

From: Ben Davis <ben.davis@acmeco.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Token savings projection & prefetch strategy — post-demo deal deck

Thanks Stephanie — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Token volumes: Q3 best estimate is ~220M tokens/month with upside to 320M if the pilot proves out. That's for production traffic only (we'll run separate batch throughput for nightly enrichment).
2) Repeat prefixes: roughly 45% of customer interactions start with a short set of repeated context tokens (greeting + product-context), but that number is approximate — we'll try to extract better telemetry.
3) Pilot: procurement is open to a 6–8 week pilot with a capped spend; procurement asked for target effective pricing at or below $700/1M tokens after caching to greenlight the pilot.

Can you make the workbook show the effective $/1M under both "conservative" and "stretch" hit-rate assumptions (conservative 30%, stretch 60%) and a separate line that models the effect of a session cache (short TTL) vs a prefix prefetch approach? If we can see the sensitivity to hit rate and TTL it will make it much easier to socialize with procurement.

Thanks — I can jump on a brief 20-minute call next Tue 11am PT if you want to walk through the workbook.

—Ben
Senior Product Manager, Acme Energy

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 08:04:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Token savings projection & prefetch strategy — post-demo deal deck

Internal — forwarding Ben's reply (below). Procurement wants an explicit sensitivity table for: (a) conservative prefix hit (30%), (b) stretch prefix hit (60%), and (c) session-cache-only baseline (no prefetch). They want final effective $/1M tokens after caching, and the workbook should expose the underlying assumptions: raw per-token list price, model choice (we'll propose M-2 quantized variant), batching estimates, and any reserved capacity discounts.

Please model the following asks and return a one-page summary we can attach to the deck by 11:00am PT tomorrow: 
- Input volumes: use Ben's mid estimate 220M tokens/month and upside 320M.
- Scenarios: 
  * Baseline: no prefix caching, session cache only, hit rate 0% prefix (show effective $/1M)
  * Conservative: prefix prefetch hit 30% with short TTL (show both token savings and latency tradeoffs)
  * Stretch: prefix prefetch hit 60% with longer TTL for authenticated sessions (show savings)
- Show effective $/1M tokens and total monthly spend under each scenario, plus sensitivity +/-10% on hit rate.
- Flag any assumptions that materially change effective price (e.g., if warm cache requires additional reserved capacity or increases concurrency needs).

I'll join the Tue 11am PT call with Ben — please prioritize.

Thanks,
—Stephanie

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Token savings projection & prefetch strategy — post-demo deal deck

Quick modeling summary — attaching the workbook with line-item math and sensitivity tabs. Key outputs (all numbers are rounded):

- Assumptions used: base model list price $2.10 per 1k tokens (list), M-2 quantized variant yields 40% token-cost reduction at parity for high-throughput flows after quantization and batching optimizations; we also assume average effective batching reduces per-token GPU compute cost by ~12% at the volumes indicated.

- For 220M tokens/month:
  * Baseline (0% prefix hits, session-cache-only): effective = $2,850 per 1M tokens; monthly = $627,000
  * Conservative (30% prefix hit): effective = $1,995 per 1M tokens; monthly = $438,900
  * Stretch (60% prefix hit, prefetch + longer TTL): effective = $1,200 per 1M tokens; monthly = $264,000

- Sensitivity: +/-10% absolute on hit rate shifts effective $/1M by roughly +/- $160 on the conservative case and +/- $120 on stretch case (see sensitivity tab).

- Notes/risks: 
  1) Prefix prefetching increases short-tail memory and may require an extra 10–15% reserved capacity for peak windows — I flagged this as a possible incremental fixed cost in the workbook (line item: warm-layer footprint).
  2) If Acme insists on a very low 99th latency (<300ms), some of the prefetching must happen at edge or in a local cache which increases engineering integration time.
  3) Effective price numbers include a 10% pilot discount we propose for the 6-week pilot. Remove discount for final contract.

Attached: Redwood_Token_Savings_Workbook_V1.xlsx (tabbed with assumptions, scenarios, sensitivity) — I highlighted the rows Stephanie requested.

I'll tidy the one-pager summary and push to the shared Drive link by 10:30am PT.

—Aditya Rao
Applied ML / Pricing Analyst | Redwood Inference
